Mass (or charge, population...) per unit area or volume; integrating it gives the total.
The instantaneous rate of change $f'(x) = \lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}$, the slope of the graph.

$f(x, y)$ is differentiable at a point if its linear approximation is accurate in every direction: the error goes to zero faster than the distance to the point. Continuous partial derivatives guarantee it.
The quantity $dz = f_x\,dx + f_y\,dy$, the change along the tangent plane; it approximates the actual change $\Delta z$.
A physical law stated at points using derivatives (div, curl), such as $\nabla\cdot\mathbf E = \rho/\varepsilon_0$.
The angles a vector makes with the positive coordinate axes; their cosines are the components of its unit vector.
A vector parallel to a line, used in $\mathbf r = \mathbf r_0 + t\mathbf v$.
The rate of change of $f$ in the direction of a unit vector $\mathbf u$: $D_{\mathbf u}f = \nabla f\cdot\mathbf u$.
In the second-derivative test, $D = f_{xx}f_{yy} - (f_{xy})^2$ at a critical point.
$\operatorname{div}\mathbf F = \nabla\cdot\mathbf F = P_x + Q_y + R_z$; the net outflow per unit volume at a point.
For a closed surface $S$ bounding $E$, oriented outward: $\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf S = \iiint_E\operatorname{div}\mathbf F\,dV$.
The set of inputs where a function is defined; for $f(x,y)$ it is a region in the plane.
The number $\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b = a_1b_1 + a_2b_2 + a_3b_3 = |\mathbf a||\mathbf b|\cos\theta$.
The limit of double Riemann sums $\iint_R f\,dA$; for $f \ge 0$, the volume under the surface over $R$.
A sum $\sum\sum f(x_{ij}^*, y_{ij}^*)\,\Delta A$ over a grid of small rectangles.
The quadric surface $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} + \dfrac{z^2}{c^2} = 1$; all traces are ellipses.
The quadric surface $\dfrac zc = \dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2}$: a bowl with elliptical horizontal traces and parabolic vertical traces.
Extreme Value Theorem: a continuous function on a closed, bounded set attains an absolute maximum and minimum.
A curve $\mathbf r(t)$ that follows a vector field, $\mathbf r'(t) = \mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))$; the path of a particle carried by the flow.
The surface integral $\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf n\,dS$ measuring how much of a field passes through a surface (in 2D, $\oint_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf n\,ds$ across a curve).
Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: if $F' = f$ is continuous, $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a)$.
Fundamental Theorem for Line Integrals: $\int_C\nabla f\cdot d\mathbf r = f(\mathbf r(b)) - f(\mathbf r(a))$.
For continuous $f$ on a rectangle (or box), the double (or triple) integral equals the iterated integral in any order.
A rule assigning one number $f(x, y)$ to each point $(x, y)$ of a domain in the plane.
The electric flux through a closed surface equals the enclosed charge divided by $\varepsilon_0$; in differential form $\nabla\cdot\mathbf E = \rho/\varepsilon_0$.
The vector of partial derivatives $\nabla f = \langle f_x, f_y, f_z\rangle$; it points in the direction of steepest increase and is perpendicular to level sets.
The vector field $\nabla f$ of a scalar function $f$.
For $f(x, y)$, the surface $z = f(x, y)$ in space.
For a positively oriented simple closed curve $C$ bounding $D$: $\oint_C P\,dx + Q\,dy = \iint_D(Q_x - P_y)\,dA$.
A curve on a parametric surface obtained by holding one parameter fixed.
A function whose Laplacian is zero, $\nabla^2 f = 0$.
The PDE $\partial T/\partial t = \alpha\nabla^2T$ governing heat conduction.
A space curve such as $\langle\cos t, \sin t, t\rangle$ that winds around a cylinder while rising steadily.
The matrix of second partial derivatives $\begin{bmatrix} f_{xx} & f_{xy}\\ f_{xy} & f_{yy}\end{bmatrix}$; its determinant is the discriminant $D$.
The saddle-shaped quadric $\dfrac zc = \dfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{y^2}{b^2}$, with hyperbolic horizontal traces.
The connected quadric $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} - \dfrac{z^2}{c^2} = 1$ (one minus sign).
The quadric $-\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} + \dfrac{z^2}{c^2} = 1$ (two minus signs), made of two separate pieces.
If $F(x, y, z) = 0$ and $F_z \ne 0$ at a point, then near it the equation defines $z$ as a differentiable function of $x$ and $y$.
A fluid flow with zero divergence everywhere: no net outflow from any region.
A line integral is independent of path if all paths with the same endpoints give the same value; true exactly for conservative fields (on open connected regions).
A physical law stated about whole regions using flux or circulation integrals, such as Gauss's law $\iint_S\mathbf E\cdot d\mathbf S = Q_{\text{enc}}/\varepsilon_0$.
The product rule backwards: $\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du$.
A vector field with zero curl.
An integral evaluated one variable at a time from the inside out, such as $\int_a^b\int_c^d f\,dy\,dx$.
The determinant $\dfrac{\partial(x, y)}{\partial(u, v)} = x_uy_v - x_vy_u$; its absolute value is the area scaling factor of a transformation.
A function $f(x, y) \ge 0$ with $\iint_{\mathbb R^2}f\,dA = 1$ describing two continuous random variables; $P\big((X, Y)\in D\big) = \iint_D f\,dA$.
The energy of motion $K = \tfrac12m|\mathbf v|^2$.
The scalar $\lambda$ in $\nabla f = \lambda\nabla g$, the condition for an extremum of $f$ subject to $g = k$; it equals the rate of change of the optimal value with $k$.
A thin flat plate, modeled as a plane region with a density per unit area.
$\nabla^2 f = \operatorname{div}(\nabla f) = f_{xx} + f_{yy} + f_{zz}$.
The line $y = mx + b$ whose slope and intercept minimize the sum of squared residuals $\sum(y_i - mx_i - b)^2$ for data $(x_i, y_i)$; it passes through $(\bar x, \bar y)$.
The set of points where $f(x, y) = c$ for a constant $c$.
The set of points where $f(x, y, z) = c$.
An integral along a curve: either $\int_C f\,ds$ (scalar) or $\int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r$ (vector), computed with a parametrization.
The approximation $f(x, y) \approx L(x, y)$ of a function by its linearization near a point.
$L(x, y) = f(a,b) + f_x(a,b)(x - a) + f_y(a,b)(y - b)$, the function whose graph is the tangent plane.
A point where $f$ is at least as large as at all nearby points.
A point where $f$ is at most as large as at all nearby points.
The length of a vector, $|\mathbf v| = \sqrt{v_1^2 + v_2^2 + v_3^2}$.
Total amount of matter; for a lamina $m = \iint_D\rho\,dA$, for a solid $m = \iiint_E\rho\,dV$.
For a projectile launched at speed $v_0$ and angle $\alpha$, $H = \dfrac{(v_0\sin\alpha)^2}{2g}$.
Fitting a model to data by choosing its coefficients to minimize the sum of the squared residuals, found by setting the partial derivatives of that sum to zero.
Mass weighted by distance from an axis (or plane), e.g. $M_y = \iint x\rho\,dA$; used to locate the center of mass.
Mass weighted by squared distance from an axis, e.g. $I_0 = \iint(x^2 + y^2)\rho\,dA$; resistance to rotational acceleration.
Force equals mass times acceleration, $\mathbf F = m\mathbf a$.
For acceleration, $a_N = \kappa v^2 = |\mathbf r'\times\mathbf r''|/|\mathbf r'|$, the part that changes direction. For a field on a surface, $\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf n$.
The linear equations for the least squares line, from $S_m = 0$ and $S_b = 0$: $m\sum x_i^2 + b\sum x_i = \sum x_iy_i$ and $m\sum x_i + nb = \sum y_i$.
The line through a point of a surface in the direction of the normal vector, e.g. $\mathbf r_0 + t\nabla F(P)$.
A vector perpendicular to a plane or surface; for $ax + by + cz = d$ it is $\langle a, b, c\rangle$, for a parametric surface $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$.
A surface on which a unit normal can be chosen continuously everywhere (a Möbius strip is not orientable).
A choice of direction: of travel along a curve, or of unit normal on a surface. Reversing it flips the sign of vector line integrals and flux.
Perpendicular; two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is 0.
The circle that best fits a curve at a point, on its concave side, with radius $1/\kappa$.
The plane spanned by $\mathbf T$ and $\mathbf N$ at a point of a curve; its normal is $\mathbf B$.
Two nonzero vectors are parallel when one is a scalar multiple of the other (equivalently, their cross product is $\mathbf 0$).
A slanted box with edges $\mathbf a, \mathbf b, \mathbf c$; its volume is $|\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf b\times\mathbf c)|$.
A curve given by coordinates as functions of a parameter, $x = x(t)$, $y = y(t)$.
Equations $x = x_0 + at$, $y = y_0 + bt$, $z = z_0 + ct$ giving each coordinate of a line (or curve) in terms of a parameter.
A surface given by $\mathbf r(u, v) = \langle x(u,v), y(u,v), z(u,v)\rangle$ for $(u, v)$ in a region $D$.
The derivative of $f$ with respect to one variable with the others held constant, e.g. $f_x = \partial f/\partial x$.
Partial differential equation: an equation relating an unknown function to its partial derivatives, such as the heat equation $u_t = u_{xx}$.
A mechanical instrument that measures the area of a region by tracing its boundary, an application of Green's theorem.
Coordinates $(r, \theta)$ with $x = r\cos\theta$, $y = r\sin\theta$; area element $dA = r\,dr\,d\theta$.
A region $a \le r \le b$, $\alpha \le \theta \le \beta$: a sector of a ring.
The vector from the origin to a point; $\langle x, y, z\rangle$ for the point $(x, y, z)$.
For a closed curve bounding a region, counterclockwise (region on the left); for the boundary of a surface, the direction given by the right-hand rule.
A function $U$ with $\mathbf F = -\nabla U$ for a conservative force; the work done equals the loss of $U$.
A scalar function $f$ with $\nabla f = \mathbf F$.
The unit vector $\mathbf N = \mathbf T'/|\mathbf T'|$ pointing in the direction a curve is turning.
The shadow of a curve or solid on a coordinate plane, obtained by dropping a coordinate; for a solid, the region $D$ over which the outer integrals run.
The graph of a second-degree equation in $x, y, z$: ellipsoids, paraboloids, cones and hyperboloids.
A vector field pointing along the position vector (directly toward or away from the origin) at every point.
The reciprocal $\rho = 1/\kappa$ of the curvature: the radius of the osculating circle.
The set of output values of a function. (For a projectile, "range" also means the horizontal distance traveled, $v_0^2\sin2\alpha/g$ on level ground.)
Observed minus predicted value for a data point, $e_i = y_i - (mx_i + b)$: the vertical gap between the point and a fitted line.
The sum of several forces (or other vectors) acting together.
Curl the fingers of the right hand from the first direction to the second; the thumb gives the third (orientation of axes, $\mathbf a\times\mathbf b$, and boundary orientation in Stokes' theorem).
A critical point where $f$ takes both larger and smaller values arbitrarily close by; the second-derivative test gives $D < 0$.
A real number, as opposed to a vector.
The equation $ax + by + cz = d$ of a plane, whose coefficients give a normal vector.
The integral $\int_C f\,ds = \int_a^b f(\mathbf r(t))|\mathbf r'(t)|\,dt$; independent of direction.
The signed length of the shadow of $\mathbf b$ on the line of $\mathbf a$: $\operatorname{comp}_{\mathbf a}\mathbf b = \dfrac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf a|}$.
The number $\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf b\times\mathbf c)$, a $3\times3$ determinant; its absolute value is the volume of a parallelepiped.
At a critical point with $D = f_{xx}f_{yy} - f_{xy}^2$: $D > 0, f_{xx} > 0$ min; $D > 0, f_{xx} < 0$ max; $D < 0$ saddle; $D = 0$ inconclusive.
Partial derivatives of partial derivatives: $f_{xx}, f_{xy}, f_{yx}, f_{yy}$.
A closed curve that does not cross itself.
A connected region in which every simple closed curve encloses only points of the region (no holes).
A point where a field has negative divergence: more flows in than out.
Lines in space that are not parallel and do not intersect.
Having continuous derivatives and a nonzero tangent or normal: for a parametric surface, $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v \ne \mathbf 0$.
A point where a field has positive divergence: more flows out than in.
The curve traced by the tip of a vector function $\mathbf r(t)$ in space.
The length of the velocity vector, $|\mathbf r'(t)| = ds/dt$.
All points at distance $r$ from a center $(h, k, l)$: $(x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 + (z-l)^2 = r^2$.
Coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ with $x = \rho\sin\phi\cos\theta$, $y = \rho\sin\phi\sin\theta$, $z = \rho\cos\phi$; $dV = \rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\theta\,d\phi$.
The unit vectors $\mathbf i = \langle 1,0,0\rangle$, $\mathbf j = \langle 0,1,0\rangle$, $\mathbf k = \langle 0,0,1\rangle$ along the axes.
For an oriented surface $S$ with boundary $C$ (right-hand rule): $\oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r = \iint_S\operatorname{curl}\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf S$.
The chain rule backwards: with $u = g(x)$, $\int f(g(x))g'(x)\,dx = \int f(u)\,du$ (change the limits too).
The total misfit of a model to data, $S = \sum e_i^2$, the sum of the squared residuals; least squares minimizes it.
$dS = |\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v|\,du\,dv$, the area of a small patch of a parametric surface.
Equations $\dfrac{x - x_0}{a} = \dfrac{y - y_0}{b} = \dfrac{z - z_0}{c}$ of a line, from solving the parametric equations for $t$.
Touching a curve and pointing along it; $\mathbf r'(t)$ is tangent to the curve $\mathbf r(t)$.
The plane that best approximates a surface at a point: $z = f(a,b) + f_x(a,b)(x - a) + f_y(a,b)(y - b)$.

glossary.term: tangent plane to a level surface
glossary.definition: At $P$ on $F(x, y, z) = k$, the plane $\nabla F(P)\cdot\langle x - x_0, y - y_0, z - z_0\rangle = 0$.
The derivative $\mathbf r'(t)$, which points along the curve in the direction of motion.
The part of a vector along the direction of motion: $a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf r'\cdot\mathbf r''}{|\mathbf r'|}$ for acceleration, $\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf T$ for a field along a curve.
The system of ordered triples $(x, y, z)$ on three mutually perpendicular axes oriented by the right-hand rule.
For a projectile over level ground, $t = \dfrac{2v_0\sin\alpha}{g}$.
The moving frame of unit tangent $\mathbf T$, principal normal $\mathbf N$ and binormal $\mathbf B$ along a curve.
The turning effect of a force: $\boldsymbol\tau = \mathbf r\times\mathbf F$.
The rate $\tau$ at which a curve twists out of its osculating plane, defined by $d\mathbf B/ds = -\tau\mathbf N$.
The curve in which a surface meets a plane, usually one parallel to a coordinate plane.
A map $T(u, v) = (x(u,v), y(u,v))$ from one plane to another, used for changes of variables.
A diagram of dependencies used with the chain rule: multiply derivatives along each path and add over paths.
The integral $\iiint_E f\,dV$ of a function over a solid region.
A solid lying between two surfaces $z = u_1(x, y)$ and $z = u_2(x, y)$ over a region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.
A plane region $a \le x \le b$, $g_1(x) \le y \le g_2(x)$ (between two graphs of $x$).
A plane region $c \le y \le d$, $h_1(y) \le x \le h_2(y)$ (between two graphs of $y$).
$\mathbf T(t) = \mathbf r'(t)/|\mathbf r'(t)|$.
A vector of length 1; $\mathbf v/|\mathbf v|$ is the unit vector in the direction of $\mathbf v$.
A quantity with length and direction, written $\langle v_1, v_2, v_3\rangle$.
The calculus of vector fields: line and surface integrals, curl, divergence, and the theorems of Green, Stokes and Gauss.
A function assigning a vector $\mathbf F(x, y) = \langle P, Q\rangle$ (or $\langle P, Q, R\rangle$ in space) to each point.
The integral $\int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r = \int_a^b\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))\cdot\mathbf r'(t)\,dt$; it changes sign when the direction is reversed.
The vector $\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf a}\mathbf b = \dfrac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf a|^2}\mathbf a$, the part of $\mathbf b$ along $\mathbf a$.
A function $\mathbf r(t) = \langle f(t), g(t), h(t)\rangle$ that outputs a vector for each value of $t$.
The derivative of position, $\mathbf v(t) = \mathbf r'(t)$; a vector tangent to the path.
Force times displacement along the motion: $\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf D$ for a constant force, $\int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r$ in general.
A sum of function values times small lengths, areas or volumes; its limit defines the integral.
A one-sided surface made by giving a strip a half twist before joining its ends; it is not orientable.
The four laws of electromagnetism (Gauss for $\mathbf E$ and $\mathbf B$, Faraday, Ampère–Maxwell), in integral or differential form.
Heat flux is proportional to minus the temperature gradient: $\mathbf q = -k\nabla T$.
A changing magnetic flux induces circulation of the electric field: $\nabla\times\mathbf E = -\partial\mathbf B/\partial t$.

references.title: Differential calculus formulas
references.body:
## Single-variable review

| Rule | Formula |
|---|---|
| Chain rule | $\frac{d}{dx}f(g(x)) = f'(g(x))g'(x)$ |
| Product, quotient | $(fg)' = f'g + fg'$, $(f/g)' = (f'g - fg')/g^2$ |
| FTC | $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a)$ where $F' = f$ |
| Parts | $\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du$ |
| Polar | $x = r\cos\theta$, $y = r\sin\theta$; area $\tfrac12\int r^2\,d\theta$ |

## Vector functions and motion

| Quantity | Formula |
|---|---|
| Velocity, speed, acceleration | $\mathbf v = \mathbf r'$, $\lvert\mathbf r'\rvert$, $\mathbf a = \mathbf r''$ |
| Arc length | $L = \int_a^b\lvert\mathbf r'(t)\rvert\,dt$ |
| Unit tangent | $\mathbf T = \mathbf r'/\lvert\mathbf r'\rvert$ |
| Principal normal, binormal | $\mathbf N = \mathbf T'/\lvert\mathbf T'\rvert$, $\mathbf B = \mathbf T\times\mathbf N$ |
| Curvature | $\kappa = \dfrac{\lvert\mathbf T'\rvert}{\lvert\mathbf r'\rvert} = \dfrac{\lvert\mathbf r'\times\mathbf r''\rvert}{\lvert\mathbf r'\rvert^3}$; for $y = f(x)$: $\dfrac{\lvert f''\rvert}{(1 + f'^2)^{3/2}}$ |
| Acceleration components | $a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf r'\cdot\mathbf r''}{\lvert\mathbf r'\rvert}$, $a_N = \dfrac{\lvert\mathbf r'\times\mathbf r''\rvert}{\lvert\mathbf r'\rvert} = \kappa v^2$ |
| Projectile | $\mathbf r = \langle v_0t\cos\alpha,\; v_0t\sin\alpha - \tfrac12gt^2\rangle$ |
| Range, flight time, height | $\dfrac{v_0^2\sin2\alpha}{g}$, $\dfrac{2v_0\sin\alpha}{g}$, $\dfrac{(v_0\sin\alpha)^2}{2g}$ |

## Partial derivatives

| Idea | Formula |
|---|---|
| Tangent plane | $z = f(a,b) + f_x(a,b)(x-a) + f_y(a,b)(y-b)$ |
| Differential | $dz = f_x\,dx + f_y\,dy$ |
| Chain rule | $\dfrac{dz}{dt} = f_x\dfrac{dx}{dt} + f_y\dfrac{dy}{dt}$; one term per tree path |
| Implicit | $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{F_x}{F_y}$; $\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x} = -\dfrac{F_x}{F_z}$ |
| Gradient | $\nabla f = \langle f_x, f_y, f_z\rangle$ |
| Directional derivative | $D_{\mathbf u}f = \nabla f\cdot\mathbf u$ ($\lvert\mathbf u\rvert = 1$); max $\lvert\nabla f\rvert$ |
| Level surface tangent plane | $\nabla F(P)\cdot\langle x-x_0, y-y_0, z-z_0\rangle = 0$ |
| Clairaut | $f_{xy} = f_{yx}$ when both are continuous near the point |

## Optimization

| Tool | Statement |
|---|---|
| Critical point | $\nabla f = \mathbf 0$ or undefined |
| Second-derivative test | At a critical point with continuous second partials, $D = f_{xx}f_{yy} - f_{xy}^2$: $D>0, f_{xx}>0$ min; $D>0, f_{xx}<0$ max; $D<0$ saddle; $D=0$ inconclusive |
| Closed region | Compare interior critical values with boundary extremes (include corners) |
| Lagrange | $\nabla f = \lambda\nabla g$, $g = k$ (needs $\nabla g \ne \mathbf 0$); two constraints: $\nabla f = \lambda\nabla g + \mu\nabla h$ ($\nabla g$, $\nabla h$ not parallel) |
| Least squares line | Minimize $S(m,b) = \sum(y_i - mx_i - b)^2$; normal equations $m\sum x_i^2 + b\sum x_i = \sum x_iy_i$, $m\sum x_i + nb = \sum y_i$ |
| Least squares formulas | $m = \dfrac{n\sum x_iy_i - \sum x_i\sum y_i}{n\sum x_i^2 - (\sum x_i)^2}$, $b = \bar y - m\bar x$; through the origin: $k = \sum x_iy_i/\sum x_i^2$ |

references.title: Multiple integrals and coordinate systems
references.body:
## Setting up

| Region | Integral |
|---|---|
| Rectangle | $\int_a^b\int_c^d f\,dy\,dx$ (either order, Fubini) |
| Type I | $\int_a^b\int_{g_1(x)}^{g_2(x)}f\,dy\,dx$ |
| Type II | $\int_c^d\int_{h_1(y)}^{h_2(y)}f\,dx\,dy$ |
| Type 1 solid | $\iint_D\int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)}f\,dz\,dA$ |

Outer limits are constants; inner limits depend only on outer variables. To reverse the
order, sketch the region and slice the other way.

## Coordinate systems

| System | Conversion | Element |
|---|---|---|
| Polar | $x = r\cos\theta$, $y = r\sin\theta$ | $dA = r\,dr\,d\theta$ |
| Cylindrical | $x = r\cos\theta$, $y = r\sin\theta$, $z = z$ | $dV = r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta$ |
| Spherical | $x = \rho\sin\phi\cos\theta$, $y = \rho\sin\phi\sin\theta$, $z = \rho\cos\phi$ | $dV = \rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\theta\,d\phi$ |
| General | $x = x(u,v)$, $y = y(u,v)$ | $dA = \left\lvert\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right\rvert du\,dv$ |

Ranges: $0 \le \theta \le 2\pi$, $0 \le \phi \le \pi$. Surfaces: $r = c$ cylinder, $z = r$ cone,
$\rho = c$ sphere, $\phi = c$ cone.

Jacobian: $\dfrac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)} = x_uy_v - x_vy_u = 1\Big/\dfrac{\partial(u,v)}{\partial(x,y)}$.

## Applications

| Quantity | Lamina ($dA$) | Solid ($dV$) |
|---|---|---|
| Area / volume | $\iint_D 1\,dA$ | $\iiint_E 1\,dV$ |
| Mass | $\iint_D\rho\,dA$ | $\iiint_E\rho\,dV$ |
| Moments | $M_y = \iint x\rho$, $M_x = \iint y\rho$ | $M_{yz} = \iiint x\rho$, $M_{xz} = \iiint y\rho$, $M_{xy} = \iiint z\rho$ |
| Center of mass | $\bar x = M_y/m$, $\bar y = M_x/m$ | $\bar x = M_{yz}/m$, $\bar y = M_{xz}/m$, $\bar z = M_{xy}/m$ |
| Average value | $\frac{1}{A}\iint f\,dA$ | $\frac1V\iiint f\,dV$ |
| Moment of inertia | $I_0 = \iint(x^2+y^2)\rho\,dA$ | $I_z = \iiint(x^2+y^2)\rho\,dV$ |
| Surface area of $z = f(x,y)$ | $\iint_D\sqrt{1 + f_x^2 + f_y^2}\,dA$ | |
| Probability (joint density $f$) | $P\big((X,Y)\in D\big) = \iint_D f\,dA$, $E(X) = \iint x f\,dA$ | |

## Useful values

| Integral | Value |
|---|---|
| $\int_0^{2\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta = \int_0^{2\pi}\cos^2\theta\,d\theta$ | $\pi$ |
| $\int_0^\pi\sin\phi\,d\phi$ | $2$ |
| $\int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-x^2}\,dx$ | $\sqrt\pi$ |
| Ball, radius $a$ | $V = \tfrac43\pi a^3$, surface $4\pi a^2$ |
| Tetrahedron $\frac xa + \frac yb + \frac zc \le 1$ | $V = abc/6$ |
| Half-disk centroid | $\bar y = 4a/(3\pi)$ |
| Solid hemisphere centroid | $\bar z = 3a/8$ |

references.title: Vector calculus and the big theorems
references.body:
## Operators

| Operator | Formula | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Gradient | $\nabla f = \langle f_x, f_y, f_z\rangle$ | vector |
| Divergence | $\nabla\cdot\mathbf F = P_x + Q_y + R_z$ | scalar |
| Curl | $\nabla\times\mathbf F = \langle R_y - Q_z,\; P_z - R_x,\; Q_x - P_y\rangle$ | vector |
| Laplacian | $\nabla^2 f = f_{xx} + f_{yy} + f_{zz}$ | scalar |

Identities: $\nabla\times(\nabla f) = \mathbf 0$, $\nabla\cdot(\nabla\times\mathbf F) = 0$.

## Line and surface integrals

| Integral | Computation |
|---|---|
| $\int_C f\,ds$ | $\int_a^b f(\mathbf r(t))\lvert\mathbf r'(t)\rvert\,dt$ |
| $\int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r$ | $\int_a^b\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))\cdot\mathbf r'(t)\,dt = \int_C P\,dx + Q\,dy + R\,dz$ |
| Surface area | $\iint_D\lvert\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\rvert\,dA$ |
| $\iint_S f\,dS$ | $\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\lvert\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\rvert\,dA$ |
| Flux $\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf S$ | $\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)\,dA$ |
| Flux, graph $z = g$ upward | $\iint_D(-Pg_x - Qg_y + R)\,dA$ |

Standard parametrizations: sphere $\langle a\sin\phi\cos\theta, a\sin\phi\sin\theta, a\cos\phi\rangle$ with
$\lvert\mathbf r_\phi\times\mathbf r_\theta\rvert = a^2\sin\phi$; cylinder $\langle a\cos\theta, a\sin\theta, z\rangle$
with factor $a$; cone $\langle r\cos\theta, r\sin\theta, r\rangle$ with factor $r\sqrt2$.

## Conservative fields

For $\mathbf F$ with continuous first partials on an open, simply connected region, the following are equivalent:
$\mathbf F = \nabla f$; $\int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r$ is path independent; $\oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r = 0$
for every closed $C$; $P_y = Q_x$ (2D) or $\nabla\times\mathbf F = \mathbf 0$ (3D).

Find $f$: integrate $P$ in $x$, add $g(y, z)$, match the other components.

## The fundamental theorems

| Theorem | Statement |
|---|---|
| FTC | $\int_a^b F'(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a)$ |
| Line integrals | $\int_C\nabla f\cdot d\mathbf r = f(\mathbf r(b)) - f(\mathbf r(a))$ |
| Green (circulation) | $\oint_C P\,dx + Q\,dy = \iint_D(Q_x - P_y)\,dA$ |
| Green (flux) | $\oint_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf n\,ds = \iint_D(P_x + Q_y)\,dA$ |
| Stokes | $\oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r = \iint_S(\nabla\times\mathbf F)\cdot d\mathbf S$ |
| Divergence (Gauss) | $\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf S = \iiint_E\nabla\cdot\mathbf F\,dV$ |

Orientation: Green, counterclockwise; Stokes, right-hand rule (thumb along $\mathbf n$);
Divergence, outward normal on a closed surface. Area: $A = \tfrac12\oint_C x\,dy - y\,dx$.

## Physics

| Law | Integral form | Differential form |
|---|---|---|
| Gauss | $\iint_S\mathbf E\cdot d\mathbf S = Q/\varepsilon_0$ | $\nabla\cdot\mathbf E = \rho/\varepsilon_0$ |
| No monopoles | $\iint_S\mathbf B\cdot d\mathbf S = 0$ | $\nabla\cdot\mathbf B = 0$ |
| Faraday | $\oint\mathbf E\cdot d\mathbf r = -\frac{d}{dt}\iint\mathbf B\cdot d\mathbf S$ | $\nabla\times\mathbf E = -\partial_t\mathbf B$ |
| Ampère (steady) | $\oint\mathbf B\cdot d\mathbf r = \mu_0I$ | $\nabla\times\mathbf B = \mu_0\mathbf J$ |
| Continuity | $\frac{d}{dt}\iiint\rho\,dV = -\iint\rho\mathbf v\cdot d\mathbf S$ | $\partial_t\rho + \nabla\cdot(\rho\mathbf v) = 0$ |
| Heat | $\mathbf q = -k\nabla T$ | $T_t = \alpha\nabla^2T$ |

references.title: Vectors, lines, planes and surfaces
references.body:
## Vectors

| Quantity | Formula |
|---|---|
| Distance | $\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2 + (z_2-z_1)^2}$ |
| Sphere | $(x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 + (z-l)^2 = r^2$ |
| Magnitude | $\lvert\mathbf v\rvert = \sqrt{v_1^2 + v_2^2 + v_3^2}$ |
| Unit vector | $\mathbf v/\lvert\mathbf v\rvert$ |
| Dot product | $\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b = a_1b_1 + a_2b_2 + a_3b_3 = \lvert\mathbf a\rvert\lvert\mathbf b\rvert\cos\theta$ |
| Angle | $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{\lvert\mathbf a\rvert\lvert\mathbf b\rvert}$ |
| Scalar projection | $\operatorname{comp}_{\mathbf a}\mathbf b = \dfrac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{\lvert\mathbf a\rvert}$ |
| Vector projection | $\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf a}\mathbf b = \dfrac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{\lvert\mathbf a\rvert^2}\mathbf a$ |
| Cross product | $\langle a_2b_3 - a_3b_2,\; a_3b_1 - a_1b_3,\; a_1b_2 - a_2b_1\rangle$ |
| $\lvert\mathbf a\times\mathbf b\rvert$ | $\lvert\mathbf a\rvert\lvert\mathbf b\rvert\sin\theta$ = parallelogram area |
| Triangle area | $\tfrac12\lvert\overrightarrow{PQ}\times\overrightarrow{PR}\rvert$ |
| Triple product | $\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf b\times\mathbf c) = \det[\mathbf a; \mathbf b; \mathbf c]$; volume $= \lvert\cdot\rvert$ |
| Work (constant force) | $W = \mathbf F\cdot\mathbf D$ |
| Torque | $\boldsymbol\tau = \mathbf r\times\mathbf F$ |

Tests: orthogonal ⇔ $\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b = 0$; parallel ⇔ $\mathbf a\times\mathbf b = \mathbf 0$; coplanar ⇔ triple product $= 0$.

## Lines and planes

| Object | Equation |
|---|---|
| Line | $\mathbf r = \mathbf r_0 + t\mathbf v$; $x = x_0 + at$, $y = y_0 + bt$, $z = z_0 + ct$ |
| Symmetric form | $\dfrac{x-x_0}{a} = \dfrac{y-y_0}{b} = \dfrac{z-z_0}{c}$ |
| Segment $\mathbf r_0 \to \mathbf r_1$ | $(1-t)\mathbf r_0 + t\mathbf r_1$, $0 \le t \le 1$ |
| Plane | $a(x-x_0) + b(y-y_0) + c(z-z_0) = 0$, normal $\langle a,b,c\rangle$ |
| Plane through $P, Q, R$ | normal $\overrightarrow{PQ}\times\overrightarrow{PR}$ |
| Line of two planes | direction $\mathbf n_1\times\mathbf n_2$ |
| Point to plane $ax + by + cz = d$ | $D = \dfrac{\lvert ax_1 + by_1 + cz_1 - d\rvert}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}}$ |

## Quadric surfaces

| Surface | Equation | Traces |
|---|---|---|
| Ellipsoid | $\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} + \frac{z^2}{c^2} = 1$ | ellipses |
| Elliptic paraboloid | $\frac zc = \frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2}$ | ellipses, parabolas |
| Hyperbolic paraboloid | $\frac zc = \frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2}$ | hyperbolas, parabolas |
| Cone | $\frac{z^2}{c^2} = \frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2}$ | ellipses, hyperbolas (line pairs through the axis) |
| Hyperboloid, one sheet | $\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} - \frac{z^2}{c^2} = 1$ | ellipses, hyperbolas |
| Hyperboloid, two sheets | $-\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} + \frac{z^2}{c^2} = 1$ | ellipses ($\lvert z\rvert > c$), hyperbolas |

A missing variable means a cylinder parallel to that axis.

drills.title: Product rule with an exponential
drills.prompt: Differentiate $f(x) = x^{n}e^{{k:coef}x}$.
drills.solution:
Product rule with $u = x^{n}$ and $v = e^{{k:coef}x}$: $u' = {n}x^{nm1}$ and, by the chain rule, $v' = {k:coef}e^{{k:coef}x}$.
So $f'(x) = u'v + uv' =$ **${n}x^{nm1}e^{{k:coef}x} {k:signedcoef}x^{n}e^{{k:coef}x}$**.

drills.title: Definite integral by substitution
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{a} x\,(x^2 + {k})^{n}\,dx$. (Exact fraction or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Let $u = x^2 + {k}$, so $du = 2x\,dx$. The limits become $u = {k}$ and $u = {top}$:
$\dfrac12\displaystyle\int_{{k}}^{{top}} u^{n}\,du = \dfrac{u^{{n1}}}{2\cdot {n1}}\Big|_{{k}}^{{top}} = \dfrac{{top}^{{n1}} - {k}^{{n1}}}{{den}} =$ **{ans}**.

drills.title: Distance between points in space
drills.prompt: Find the distance between $P({x1}, {y1}, {z1})$ and $Q({x2}, {y2}, {z2})$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Differences: $\Delta x = {dx}$, $\Delta y = {dy}$, $\Delta z = {dz}$.
$|PQ| = \sqrt{({dx})^2 + ({dy})^2 + ({dz})^2} = \sqrt{{s}} \approx$ **{dist:num2}**.

drills.title: Linear combination of vectors
drills.prompt: Let $\mathbf u = \langle {u1}, {u2}, {u3}\rangle$ and $\mathbf v = \langle {v1}, {v2}, {v3}\rangle$. Find ${p:coef}\mathbf u {q:signedcoef}\mathbf v$.
drills.solution:
Scale each vector, then add componentwise:
first ${p}({u1}) + ({q})({v1}) = {w1}$, second ${p}({u2}) + ({q})({v2}) = {w2}$, third ${p}({u3}) + ({q})({v3}) = {w3}$.
Result: **$\langle {w1}, {w2}, {w3}\rangle$**.

drills.title: Unit vector in a given direction
drills.prompt: Find the unit vector in the direction of $\mathbf v = \langle {v1}, {v2}, {v3}\rangle$. (Exact fractions.)
drills.solution:
$|\mathbf v| = \sqrt{({v1})^2 + ({v2})^2 + ({v3})^2} = {L}$. Divide each component by {L}:
**$\left\langle {e1:texfrac}, {e2:texfrac}, {e3:texfrac}\right\rangle$**.

drills.title: Angle between two vectors
drills.prompt: Find the angle between $\mathbf a = \langle {a1}, {a2}, {a3}\rangle$ and $\mathbf b = \langle {b1}, {b2}, {b3}\rangle$, in degrees (1 decimal).
drills.solution:
$\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b = {dot}$, $|\mathbf a| \approx {la:num4}$, $|\mathbf b| \approx {lb:num4}$.
$\cos\theta = \dfrac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf a||\mathbf b|} \approx {cs:num4}$, so $\theta \approx$ **{ang:num1}°**.

drills.title: Vector projection
drills.prompt: Find $\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf a}\mathbf b$ for $\mathbf a = \langle {a1}, {a2}, {a3}\rangle$ and $\mathbf b = \langle {b1}, {b2}, {b3}\rangle$. (Exact fractions.)
drills.solution:
$\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b = {dot}$ and $|\mathbf a|^2 = {aa}$, so $\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf a}\mathbf b = {f:texfrac}\,\mathbf a =$
**$\left\langle {p1:texfrac}, {p2:texfrac}, {p3:texfrac}\right\rangle$**.

drills.title: Compute a cross product
drills.prompt: Compute $\mathbf a\times\mathbf b$ for $\mathbf a = \langle {a1}, {a2}, {a3}\rangle$ and $\mathbf b = \langle {b1}, {b2}, {b3}\rangle$.

drills.title: Area of a triangle in space
drills.prompt: Find the area of the triangle with vertices $P({px}, {py}, {pz})$, $Q({qx}, {qy}, {qz})$, $R({rx}, {ry}, {rz})$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\overrightarrow{PQ} = \langle {u1}, {u2}, {u3}\rangle$, $\overrightarrow{PR} = \langle {v1}, {v2}, {v3}\rangle$.
$\overrightarrow{PQ}\times\overrightarrow{PR} = \langle {c1}, {c2}, {c3}\rangle$, and half its length is the area: $\tfrac12\sqrt{({c1})^2 + ({c2})^2 + ({c3})^2} \approx$ **{area:num2}**.

drills.title: Volume of a parallelepiped
drills.prompt: Find the volume of the parallelepiped with edges $\mathbf a = \langle {a1}, {a2}, {a3}\rangle$, $\mathbf b = \langle {b1}, {b2}, {b3}\rangle$, $\mathbf c = \langle {c1}, {c2}, {c3}\rangle$.
drills.solution:
$\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf b\times\mathbf c) = \begin{vmatrix} {a1} & {a2} & {a3}\\ {b1} & {b2} & {b3}\\ {c1} & {c2} & {c3}\end{vmatrix} = {det}$.
The volume is its absolute value: **{vol}**.

drills.title: Plane through three points
drills.prompt: Find the plane through $P({px}, {py}, {pz})$, $Q({qx}, {qy}, {qz})$, $R({rx}, {ry}, {rz})$. Use the normal $\mathbf n = \overrightarrow{PQ}\times\overrightarrow{PR}$ and write the plane as $n_1x + n_2y + n_3z = d$.
drills.solution:
$\overrightarrow{PQ} = \langle {u1}, {u2}, {u3}\rangle$ and $\overrightarrow{PR} = \langle {v1}, {v2}, {v3}\rangle$, so $\mathbf n = \langle {n1}, {n2}, {n3}\rangle$.
Then $d = \mathbf n\cdot P = ({n1})({px}) + ({n2})({py}) + ({n3})({pz}) = {d}$.
The plane is **${n1:coef}x {n2:signedcoef}y {n3:signedcoef}z = {d}$**.

drills.title: Distance from a point to a plane
drills.prompt: Find the distance from $({x1}, {y1}, {z1})$ to the plane ${a:coef}x {b:signedcoef}y {c:signedcoef}z = {d}$. (2 decimals.)

drills.title: Center and radius of a sphere
drills.prompt: Find the center $(h, k, l)$ and radius $r$ of the sphere $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 {m1:signedcoef}x {m2:signedcoef}y {m3:signedcoef}z {cst:signed} = 0$.
drills.solution:
Complete the square in each variable: each center coordinate is minus half that variable's linear coefficient,
so $h = -\tfrac12({m1}) = {h}$, $k = -\tfrac12({m2}) = {k}$ and $l = -\tfrac12({m3}) = {l}$.
Then $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 + (z - l)^2 = h^2 + k^2 + l^2 - ({cst}) = {r}^2$.
Center **$({h}, {k}, {l})$**, radius **{r}**.

drills.title: Derivative of a vector function
drills.prompt: Find $\mathbf r'(t)$ for $\mathbf r(t) = \left\langle {a}t^{n},\; e^{{b:coef}t},\; \sin({c}t)\right\rangle$. Enter each component as an expression in $t$.
drills.solution:
Differentiate each component separately.
$\dfrac{d}{dt}\left({a}t^{n}\right) = {an}t^{{nm1}}$; $\dfrac{d}{dt}e^{{b:coef}t} = {b:coef}e^{{b:coef}t}$ (chain rule); $\dfrac{d}{dt}\sin({c}t) = {c}\cos({c}t)$ (chain rule).
So $\mathbf r'(t) =$ **$\left\langle {an}t^{{nm1}},\; {b:coef}e^{{b:coef}t},\; {c}\cos({c}t)\right\rangle$**.

drills.title: Position from velocity
drills.prompt: A particle has velocity $\mathbf r'(t) = \langle {ta}t,\; {tb}t^2,\; {c}\rangle$ and starts at $\mathbf r(0) = \langle {x0}, {y0}, {z0}\rangle$. Find its position at $t = {tt}$.
drills.solution:
Integrate each component and add the starting position: $\mathbf r(t) = \langle {a:coef}t^2 {x0:signed},\; {b:coef}t^3 {y0:signed},\; {c:coef}t {z0:signed}\rangle$.
At $t = {tt}$: **$\langle {X}, {Y}, {Z}\rangle$**.

drills.title: Length of a helix
drills.prompt: Find the length of the helix $\mathbf r(t) = \langle {R:coef}\cos t,\; {R:coef}\sin t,\; {h:coef}t\rangle$ for $0 \le t \le {tmax}\pi$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\mathbf r'(t) = \langle -{R:coef}\sin t,\; {R:coef}\cos t,\; {h}\rangle$, so $|\mathbf r'(t)| = \sqrt{{R}^2\sin^2t + {R}^2\cos^2t + {h}^2} = \sqrt{{R}^2 + {h}^2} \approx {sp:num4}$, a constant speed.
$L = \displaystyle\int_0^{{tmax}\pi}\sqrt{{R}^2 + {h}^2}\,dt = {tmax}\pi\sqrt{{R}^2 + {h}^2} \approx$ **{L:num2}**.

drills.title: Curvature of a parabola
drills.prompt: Find the curvature of $y = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x$ at $x = {x0}$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$f'(x) = {ta}x {b:signed}$ gives $f'({x0}) = {slope}$, and $f''(x) = {ta}$.
$\kappa = \dfrac{|f''|}{(1 + f'^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{|{ta}|}{(1 + ({slope})^2)^{3/2}} \approx$ **{kap:num2}**. (Radius of curvature $1/\kappa \approx {rho:num2}$.)

drills.title: Tangential and normal acceleration
drills.prompt: A particle moves along $\mathbf r(t) = \langle {a:coef}t,\; {b:coef}t^2,\; {c:coef}t\rangle$. Find the tangential and normal components of its acceleration at $t = {t0}$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\mathbf r'({t0}) = \langle {a}, {v2}, {c}\rangle$ with length $\approx {sp:num4}$, and $\mathbf r''({t0}) = \langle 0, {tb}, 0\rangle$.
$a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf r'\cdot\mathbf r''}{|\mathbf r'|} = \dfrac{({v2})({tb})}{{sp:num4}} \approx$ **{aT:num2}**.
$\mathbf r'\times\mathbf r'' = \langle {cr1}, 0, {cr3}\rangle$, so $a_N = \dfrac{|\mathbf r'\times\mathbf r''|}{|\mathbf r'|} \approx$ **{aN:num2}**.

drills.title: Projectile range, height and flight time
drills.prompt: A projectile is launched over level ground at {v0} m/s, {ang}° above the horizontal. With $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$ and no air resistance, find its flight time, range and maximum height. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Components: $v_0\cos\alpha \approx {vx:num2}$ m/s and $v_0\sin\alpha \approx {vy:num2}$ m/s.
Flight time $t = \dfrac{2v_0\sin\alpha}{g} \approx$ **{T:num2} s**.
Range $R = \dfrac{v_0^2\sin2\alpha}{g} = \dfrac{{v0}^2\sin {ang2}^\circ}{9.8} \approx$ **{R:num2} m**.
Max height $H = \dfrac{(v_0\sin\alpha)^2}{2g} \approx$ **{H:num2} m**.

drills.title: Velocity and speed
drills.prompt: A particle has position $\mathbf r(t) = \langle {p:coef}t^2,\; {q:coef}t,\; {s3:coef}t^3\rangle$. Find its velocity and speed at $t = {t0}$. (Speed to 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\mathbf v(t) = \mathbf r'(t) = \langle {tp}t,\; {q},\; {ts}t^2\rangle$, so $\mathbf v({t0}) = \langle {vx}, {vy}, {vz}\rangle$.
Speed $= \sqrt{({vx})^2 + ({vy})^2 + ({vz})^2} \approx$ **{spd:num2}**.

drills.title: Evaluate a function of two variables
drills.prompt: Evaluate $f(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2y {b:signedcoef}y^2 - {c:coef}x$ at $({x0}, {y0})$.

drills.title: Read a level curve
drills.prompt: For $f(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2 + {b:coef}y^2$, find the value $c$ of the level curve through $({x0}, {y0})$, and where that level curve crosses the positive $x$-axis (2 decimals).
drills.solution:
$c = f({x0}, {y0}) = {a}({x0})^2 + {b}({y0})^2 =$ **{c}**. The level curve ${a:coef}x^2 + {b:coef}y^2 = {c}$ is an ellipse.
On the $x$-axis $y = 0$, so $x^2 = {c}/{a}$ and $x = \sqrt{{c}/{a}} \approx$ **{sx:num2}**.

drills.title: Limit along a line
drills.prompt: Find the limit of $f(x, y) = \dfrac{{a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}y^2}{x^2 + y^2}$ as $(x, y)\to(0, 0)$ along the line $y = {m:coef}x$. (Exact fraction.)
drills.solution:
Substitute $y = {m:coef}x$: $\dfrac{{a:coef}x^2 + ({b})({m2})x^2}{(1 + {m2})x^2} = \dfrac{{num}}{{den}}$ for $x \ne 0$, so the limit along this line is **${L:texfrac}$**.
Because the answer depends on the slope (it is ${a}$ along the $x$-axis and ${b}$ along the $y$-axis), the two-variable limit does not exist.

drills.title: First partial derivatives
drills.prompt: Find $f_x$ and $f_y$ for $f(x, y) = {a}x^{m}y^{n} {b:signedcoef}xy$.
drills.solution:
For $f_x$, treat $y$ as a constant: $\partial_x\left({a}x^{m}y^{n}\right) = {am}x^{{m1}}y^{n}$ and $\partial_x({b:coef}xy) = {b:coef}y$.
For $f_y$, treat $x$ as a constant: $\partial_y\left({a}x^{m}y^{n}\right) = {an}x^{m}y^{{n1}}$ and $\partial_y({b:coef}xy) = {b:coef}x$.
**$f_x = {am}x^{{m1}}y^{n} {b:signedcoef}y$, $f_y = {an}x^{m}y^{{n1}} {b:signedcoef}x$.**

drills.title: Second partial derivatives
drills.prompt: For $f(x, y) = {a:coef}x^3y^2 {b:signedcoef}xy^3$, find $f_{xx}$, $f_{xy}$ and $f_{yy}$.
drills.solution:
First partials: $f_x = {a3}x^2y^2 {b:signedcoef}y^3$ and $f_y = {a2}x^3y {b3:signedcoef}xy^2$.
Then $f_{xx} = {a6}xy^2$, $f_{xy} = \partial_y f_x = {a6}x^2y {b3:signedcoef}y^2$ (and $f_{yx} = \partial_x f_y$ gives the same, by Clairaut), and $f_{yy} = {a2}x^3 {b6:signedcoef}xy$.
**$f_{xx} = {a6}xy^2$, $f_{xy} = {a6}x^2y {b3:signedcoef}y^2$, $f_{yy} = {a2}x^3 {b6:signedcoef}xy$.**

drills.title: Tangent plane to a graph
drills.prompt: Find the tangent plane to $z = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}y^2 {c:signedcoef}xy$ at the point where $x = {x0}$, $y = {y0}$. Write it as $z = Ax + By + C$.

drills.title: Estimate with a linearization
drills.prompt: Use the linearization of $f(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2y$ at $({x0}, {y0})$ to estimate $f({x1}, {y1})$.
drills.solution:
$f({x0}, {y0}) = {f0}$, $f_x = 2({a})xy = {fx}$, $f_y = {a:coef}x^2 = {fy}$ at the base point.
$L = {f0} + {fx}({dx}) + {fy}({dy}) =$ **{Lv:num2}**. (The exact value is about {actual:num4}.)

drills.title: Chain rule along a path
drills.prompt: Let $z = x^2 {a:signedcoef}xy$ with $x = t^2 {b:signed}$ and $y = {c:coef}t$. Use the chain rule to find $\dfrac{dz}{dt}$ at $t = {t0}$.
drills.solution:
At $t = {t0}$: $x = {X}$, $y = {Y}$.
$z_x = 2x + ({a})y = {zx}$, $z_y = ({a})x = {zy}$, $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2t = {xt}$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = {yt}$.
$\dfrac{dz}{dt} = z_x\dfrac{dx}{dt} + z_y\dfrac{dy}{dt} = ({zx})({xt}) + ({zy})({yt}) =$ **{rate}**.

drills.title: Implicit differentiation
drills.prompt: The curve $x^2 {a:signedcoef}xy + y^3 = {k}$ passes through $({x0}, {y0})$. Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ there. (Exact fraction.)
drills.solution:
With $F = x^2 + ({a})xy + y^3 - ({k})$: $F_x = 2x + ({a})y = {Fx}$ and $F_y = ({a})x + 3y^2 = {Fy}$ at the point.
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{F_x}{F_y} = -\dfrac{{Fx}}{{Fy}} =$ **${slope:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Gradient of a function of three variables
drills.prompt: Find $\nabla f$ for $f(x, y, z) = {a:coef}x^2y {b:signedcoef}yz^2 {c:signedcoef}xz$.
drills.solution:
Take each partial derivative, holding the other two variables constant:
$f_x = {a2}xy {c:signedcoef}z$, $f_y = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}z^2$, $f_z = {b2}yz {c:signedcoef}x$.
**$\nabla f = \langle {a2}xy {c:signedcoef}z,\; {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}z^2,\; {b2}yz {c:signedcoef}x\rangle$**.

drills.title: Directional derivative
drills.prompt: Find the directional derivative of $f(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}xy {c:signedcoef}y^2$ at $({x0}, {y0})$ in the direction of $\mathbf v = \langle {v1}, {v2}\rangle$. (2 decimals.)

figure.caption: The direction of v from the point

drills.solution:
$\nabla f = \langle 2({a})x + ({b})y,\; ({b})x + 2({c})y\rangle = \langle {gx}, {gy}\rangle$ at $({x0}, {y0})$.
Normalize: $|\mathbf v| = \sqrt{({v1})^2 + ({v2})^2} \approx {nv:num4}$.
$D_{\mathbf u}f = \dfrac{\nabla f\cdot\mathbf v}{|\mathbf v|} = \dfrac{({gx})({v1}) + ({gy})({v2})}{{nv:num4}} \approx$ **{D:num2}**.

drills.title: Steepest ascent
drills.prompt: For $f(x, y) = {a:coef}xy^2 {b:signedcoef}x^2$ at $({x0}, {y0})$, find the gradient and the maximum rate of increase. (Rate to 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$f_x = {a:coef}y^2 + 2({b})x = {gx}$ and $f_y = 2({a})xy = {gy}$ at the point, so $
abla f = \langle {gx}, {gy}angle$.
The maximum rate of increase is $|
abla f| = \sqrt{({gx})^2 + ({gy})^2} \approx$ **{rate:num2}**, in the direction of $
abla f$.

drills.title: Critical point of a quadratic
drills.prompt: Find the critical point of $f(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}xy {c:signedcoef}y^2 {d:signedcoef}x {e:signedcoef}y$.
drills.solution:
Set both partials to zero:
$f_x = {a2}x {b:signedcoef}y {d:signed} = 0$ and $f_y = {b:coef}x {c2:signedcoef}y {e:signed} = 0$.
Solving this linear system (for example by elimination) gives **$x = {p}$, $y = {q}$**. Check: ${a2}({p}) + ({b})({q}) + ({d}) = 0$. ✓

drills.title: Classify a critical point
drills.prompt: The point $({x0}, {y0})$ is a critical point of $f(x, y) = x^3 - {k3}x {c:signedcoef}y^2 {dd:signedcoef}y$. Find the discriminant $D$ there, and classify the point: type **1** for a local minimum, **2** for a local maximum, **3** for a saddle point.
drills.solution:
$f_{xx} = 6x = {fxx}$, $f_{yy} = {fyy}$, $f_{xy} = 0$ at $({x0}, {y0})$.
$D = f_{xx}f_{yy} - f_{xy}^2 = ({fxx})({fyy}) - 0 =$ **{D}**.
If $D < 0$ the point is a saddle; if $D > 0$, the sign of $f_{xx}$ decides (positive: minimum, negative: maximum). Answer: **type {cls}**.

drills.title: Absolute extrema on a rectangle
drills.prompt: Find the absolute maximum and minimum of $f(x, y) = (x {np:signed})^2 + (y {nq:signed})^2$ on the rectangle $0 \le x \le {A}$, $0 \le y \le {B}$.

figure.caption: f is the squared distance from ({p}, {q})

drills.solution:
$f$ is the squared distance from $({p}, {q})$. The only critical point is $({p}, {q})$ itself ($\nabla f = \mathbf 0$ there); it counts only if it lies in the rectangle.
Minimum: the closest point of the rectangle is $({p}, {q})$ if it is inside, otherwise the nearest boundary point; this gives **{fmin}**.
Maximum: on each edge $f$ is a parabola in one variable, so the largest value occurs at a corner. The farthest corner gives **{fmax}**.

drills.title: Closest point on a line (Lagrange)
drills.prompt: Use Lagrange multipliers to minimize $f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2$ subject to ${a:coef}x {b:signedcoef}y = {k}$. Give the point and the minimum value. (Exact fractions.)
drills.solution:
$\nabla f = \lambda\nabla g$: $2x = {a:coef}\lambda$ and $2y = {b:coef}\lambda$, so $x = \tfrac{{a}}{2}\lambda$, $y = \tfrac{{b}}{2}\lambda$.
Substitute into the constraint: $\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\left(({a})^2 + ({b})^2\right) = {k}$, so $\lambda = \dfrac{2\cdot{k}}{{ss}}$.
Then $x =$ **${X:texfrac}$**, $y =$ **${Y:texfrac}$**, and $f = x^2 + y^2 =$ **${fmin:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Maximize a product (Lagrange)
drills.prompt: Use Lagrange multipliers to maximize $V = xyz$ for $x, y, z > 0$ subject to ${a:coef}x + {b:coef}y + {c:coef}z = {k}$.
drills.solution:
$\nabla V = \lambda\nabla g$: $yz = {a:coef}\lambda$, $xz = {b:coef}\lambda$, $xy = {c:coef}\lambda$.
Multiply by $x$, $y$, $z$ respectively: $xyz = {a:coef}\lambda x = {b:coef}\lambda y = {c:coef}\lambda z$, so ${a:coef}x = {b:coef}y = {c:coef}z$. Each term is one third of {k}.
So ${a:coef}x = {b:coef}y = {c:coef}z = \tfrac{{k}}{3}$: **$x = {X}$, $y = {Y}$, $z = {Z}$**, and $V =$ **{V}**.

drills.title: Least squares line through four points
drills.prompt: Find the least squares line $y = mx + b$ for the points $({xa}, {y1})$, $({xb}, {y2})$, $({xc}, {y3})$, $({xd}, {y4})$. (Exact fractions, or decimals to 2 places.)
drills.solution:
Sums: $n = 4$, $\sum x_i = {sx}$, $\sum y_i = {sy}$, $\sum x_i^2 = {sxx}$, $\sum x_iy_i = {sxy}$.
Normal equations: ${sxx}m + {sx}b = {sxy}$ and ${sx}m + 4b = {sy}$.
Solving: $m = \dfrac{4({sxy}) - ({sx})({sy})}{4({sxx}) - {sx}^2} = \dfrac{{numm}}{{den}} =$ **{m:num4}**.
Then $b = \dfrac{\sum y_i - m\sum x_i}{4} = \dfrac{{sy} - ({m:num4})({sx})}{4} =$ **{b:num4}**.

drills.title: Solve the normal equations from data sums
drills.prompt: A data set of $n = {n}$ points has $\sum x_i = {sx}$, $\sum y_i = {sy}$, $\sum x_i^2 = {sxx}$ and $\sum x_iy_i = {sxy}$. Find the slope $m$ and intercept $b$ of the least squares line $y = mx + b$.
drills.solution:
The normal equations are $m\sum x_i^2 + b\sum x_i = \sum x_iy_i$ and $m\sum x_i + nb = \sum y_i$:
$${sxx}m + {sx}b = {sxy},\qquad {sx}m + {n}b = {sy}.$$
Eliminate $b$: $m = \dfrac{n\sum x_iy_i - \sum x_i\sum y_i}{n\sum x_i^2 - (\sum x_i)^2} = \dfrac{{n}({sxy}) - ({sx})({sy})}{{n}({sxx}) - {sx}^2} = \dfrac{{numm}}{{den}} =$ **{m}**.
Then $b = \left(\sum y_i - m\sum x_i\right)/n = \dfrac{{sy} - ({m})({sx})}{{n}} =$ **{b}**.

drills.title: Best line through the origin
drills.prompt: Fit the model $y = kx$, a line through the origin, to the points $({x1}, {y1})$, $({x2}, {y2})$, $({x3}, {y3})$ by least squares. (Exact fraction, or 3 decimal places.)
drills.solution:
Minimize $S(k) = \sum(y_i - kx_i)^2$. Setting $S'(k) = -2\sum x_i(y_i - kx_i) = 0$ gives $k = \dfrac{\sum x_iy_i}{\sum x_i^2}$.
$\sum x_iy_i = {x1}({y1}) + {x2}({y2}) + {x3}({y3}) = {sxy}$ and $\sum x_i^2 = {x1}^2 + {x2}^2 + {x3}^2 = {sxx}$.
So $k = \dfrac{{sxy}}{{sxx}} \approx$ **{k:dp3}**. ($S''(k) = 2\sum x_i^2 > 0$, so this is the minimum.)

drills.title: Double integral over a rectangle
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\iint_R ({p:coef}x + {q:coef}xy)\,dA$ over $R = [{a}, {b}]\times[{c}, {d}]$. (Exact or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Integrate in $y$ first, holding $x$ constant: $\displaystyle\int_{{c}}^{{d}}({p:coef}x + {q:coef}xy)\,dy = \left[{p:coef}xy + {q:coef}x\frac{y^2}{2}\right]_{y={c}}^{y={d}} = ({p}\cdot{h} + {q}\cdot{Y2})x$.
Then in $x$: $\displaystyle\int_{{a}}^{{b}}x\,dx = \frac{{b}^2 - {a}^2}{2} = {X2}$, so the value is $\left({p}\cdot{h} + {q}\cdot{Y2}\right)({X2}) =$ **{ans}**.

drills.title: Average value over a rectangle
drills.prompt: Find the average value of $f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2$ over the rectangle $[0, {A}]\times[0, {B}]$. (Exact or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\displaystyle\iint_R(x^2 + y^2)\,dA = \int_0^{{B}}\int_0^{{A}}(x^2 + y^2)\,dx\,dy = {B}\cdot\frac{{A}^3}{3} + {A}\cdot\frac{{B}^3}{3} \approx {I:num2}$.
The area is ${A}\cdot{B}$, so $f_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{{A}^2 + {B}^2}{3} \approx$ **{fav:num2}**.

drills.title: Integral over the region between a line and a parabola
drills.prompt: Let $D$ be the region between $y = x^2$ and $y = {m:coef}x$. Evaluate $\displaystyle\iint_D({p} {q:signedcoef}x)\,dA$. (Exact or 2 decimals.)

figure.caption: D lies between the parabola and the line for 0 ≤ x ≤ {m}

drills.solution:
The curves meet at $x = 0$ and $x = {m}$, with the line on top. Type I:
$\displaystyle\int_0^{{m}}\int_{x^2}^{{m:coef}x}({p} {q:signedcoef}x)\,dy\,dx = \int_0^{{m}}({p} {q:signedcoef}x)({m:coef}x - x^2)\,dx$.
Since $\int_0^{{m}}({m:coef}x - x^2)\,dx = \frac{{m}^3}{6}$ and $\int_0^{{m}}x({m:coef}x - x^2)\,dx = \frac{{m}^4}{12}$, the value is ${p}\cdot\frac{{m}^3}{6} + ({q})\cdot\frac{{m}^4}{12} =$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Reverse the order of integration
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{{top}}\int_{x/{k}}^{{b}}e^{y^2}\,dy\,dx$ by reversing the order of integration. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\int e^{y^2}\,dy$ is not elementary, so reverse. The region $0 \le x \le {top}$, $x/{k} \le y \le {b}$ is the triangle $0 \le y \le {b}$, $0 \le x \le {k}y$.
$\displaystyle\int_0^{{b}}\int_0^{{k}y}e^{y^2}\,dx\,dy = \int_0^{{b}}{k}y\,e^{y^2}\,dy = \frac{{k}}{2}\left(e^{{b}^2} - 1\right) \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Volume under a paraboloid (polar)
drills.prompt: Find the volume of the solid under $z = {H} - {k:coef}(x^2 + y^2)$ and above the $xy$-plane. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
The paraboloid meets $z = 0$ where ${k:coef}r^2 = {H}$, that is $r^2 = {R2:texfrac}$, so the base is the disk $r \le \sqrt{{R2:texfrac}}$.
$V = \displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\sqrt{{R2:texfrac}}}({H} - {k:coef}r^2)\,r\,dr\,d\theta = 2\pi\left[\frac{{H}r^2}{2} - \frac{{k:coef}r^4}{4}\right]_0^{\sqrt{{R2:texfrac}}} = \frac{\pi\cdot{H}^2}{{k2}} \approx$ **{V:num2}**.

drills.title: Area of a rose petal
drills.prompt: Find the area of one petal of the rose $r = {a:coef}\cos({n}\theta)$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
One petal runs between consecutive zeros of $\cos({n}\theta)$: $-\frac{\pi}{2\cdot{n}} \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2\cdot{n}}$.
Area $= \displaystyle\int_{-\pi/(2\cdot{n})}^{\pi/(2\cdot{n})}\int_0^{{a:coef}\cos({n}\theta)}r\,dr\,d\theta = \frac{{a}^2}{2}\int_{-\pi/(2\cdot{n})}^{\pi/(2\cdot{n})}\cos^2({n}\theta)\,d\theta = \frac{{a}^2}{2}\cdot\frac{\pi}{2\cdot{n}} \approx$ **{A:num2}**.

drills.title: Mass of a lamina
drills.prompt: A lamina occupies $[0, {A}]\times[0, {B}]$ and has density $\rho(x, y) = {p} + {q:coef}x + {s:coef}y$. Find its mass. (Exact or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution: $m = \displaystyle\int_0^{{A}}\int_0^{{B}}({p} + {q:coef}x + {s:coef}y)\,dy\,dx = {p}({A})({B}) + {q}\cdot\frac{{A}^2}{2}\cdot{B} + {s}\cdot{A}\cdot\frac{{B}^2}{2} =$ **{m:num2}**.

drills.title: Centroid of the region under a power curve
drills.prompt: Find the centroid of the region under $y = {k:coef}{n}$ for $0 \le x \le {a}$ (above the $x$-axis). (2 decimals.)

figure.caption: The region under the curve for 0 ≤ x ≤ {a}

drills.solution:
Area $A = \displaystyle\int_0^{{a}}{k:coef}{n}\,dx \approx {area:num4}$.
$\bar x = \dfrac1A\displaystyle\int_0^{{a}}x\cdot {k:coef}{n}\,dx$ and $\bar y = \dfrac1A\displaystyle\int_0^{{a}}\int_0^{{k:coef}{n}}y\,dy\,dx = \dfrac1A\int_0^{{a}}\frac{({k:coef}{n})^2}{2}\,dx$.
These give **$\bar x \approx {xb:num2}$** and **$\bar y \approx {yb:num2}$**.

drills.title: Surface area of a plane over a rectangle
drills.prompt: Find the area of the part of the plane $z = {c} {p:signedcoef}x {q:signedcoef}y$ that lies above the rectangle $[0, {A}]\times[0, {B}]$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$f_x = {p}$ and $f_y = {q}$, so the stretch factor is $\sqrt{1 + ({p})^2 + ({q})^2} \approx {fac:num4}$, constant.
Area $= \displaystyle\iint_R\sqrt{1 + f_x^2 + f_y^2}\,dA = {A}\cdot{B}\cdot{fac:num4} \approx$ **{S:num2}**.

drills.title: A joint density on a rectangle
drills.prompt: The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have joint density $f(x, y) = Cxy$ on the rectangle $0 \le x \le {a}$, $0 \le y \le {bb}$, and $0$ elsewhere. Find the constant $C$, the probability $P(X \le {s},\ Y \le {t})$, and the mean $E(X)$. (Exact fractions.)
drills.solution:
Total probability 1: $\displaystyle\int_0^{{a}}\int_0^{{bb}}Cxy\,dy\,dx = C\cdot\frac{{a2}}{2}\cdot\frac{{b2}}{2} = 1$, so $C =$ **${cc:texfrac}$**.
$P = \displaystyle\int_0^{{s}}\int_0^{{t}}Cxy\,dy\,dx = C\cdot\frac{{s}^2}{2}\cdot\frac{{t}^2}{2} =$ **${prob:texfrac}$**.
$E(X) = \displaystyle\int_0^{{a}}\int_0^{{bb}}x\cdot Cxy\,dy\,dx = C\cdot\frac{{a}^3}{3}\cdot\frac{{b2}}{2} =$ **${ex:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Triple integral over a box
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\iiint_B({p:coef}x {q:signedcoef}yz)\,dV$ over the box $B = [0, {a}]\times[0, {b}]\times[0, {c}]$. (Exact or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Split and factor each term over the box:
$\displaystyle\iiint {p:coef}x\,dV = {p}\cdot\frac{{a}^2}{2}\cdot{b}\cdot{c} = {t1}$ and $\displaystyle\iiint {q:coef}yz\,dV = ({q})\cdot{a}\cdot\frac{{b}^2}{2}\cdot\frac{{c}^2}{2} = {t2}$.
Total: **{ans}**.

drills.title: Volume and centroid height of a tetrahedron
drills.prompt: The tetrahedron $E$ is bounded by the coordinate planes and the plane $\dfrac{x}{{a}} + \dfrac{y}{{b}} + \dfrac{z}{{c}} = 1$. Find its volume and the $z$-coordinate of its centroid. (Exact or 2 decimals.)

figure.caption: Shadow on the xy-plane: 0 ≤ x ≤ {a}, 0 ≤ y ≤ {b}(1 − x/{a})

drills.solution:
Top surface $z = {c}\left(1 - \frac{x}{{a}} - \frac{y}{{b}}\right)$ over the triangle with legs {a} and {b}.
$V = \displaystyle\iint_D {c}\left(1 - \frac{x}{{a}} - \frac{y}{{b}}\right)dA = \frac{{a}\cdot{b}\cdot{c}}{6} =$ **{V:num2}**.
Likewise $\iiint_E z\,dV = \dfrac{{a}\cdot{b}\cdot{c}^2}{24}$, so $\bar z = \dfrac{{c}}{4} =$ **{zb:num2}** (the average of the vertices' heights).

drills.title: Rectangular to cylindrical
drills.prompt: Convert $({x}, {y}, {z})$ to cylindrical coordinates $(r, \theta, z)$ with $0 \le \theta < 2\pi$ ($\theta$ in radians, 2 decimals).
drills.solution:
$r = \sqrt{({x})^2 + ({y})^2} \approx {r:num2}$.
$\tan\theta = \dfrac{{y}}{{x}}$; checking the quadrant of $({x}, {y})$ gives $\theta \approx {th:num2}$ rad (about {thd:num1}°).
$z$ is unchanged. So **$(r, \theta, z) \approx ({r:num2},\ {th:num2},\ {z})$**.

drills.title: Integral over a cylinder
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\iiint_E(x^2 + y^2 {c:signedcoef}z)\,dV$, where $E$ is the solid cylinder $x^2 + y^2 \le {a}^2$, $0 \le z \le {h}$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
In cylindrical coordinates the integrand is $r^2 {c:signedcoef}z$ and $dV = r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta$:
$\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{{a}}\int_0^{{h}}(r^2 {c:signedcoef}z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta = 2\pi\left[{h}\cdot\frac{{a}^4}{4} + {c}\cdot\frac{{h}^2}{2}\cdot\frac{{a}^2}{2}\right] \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Spherical to rectangular
drills.prompt: Convert the spherical point $\rho = {rho}$, $\theta = {thd}^\circ$, $\phi = {phd}^\circ$ to rectangular coordinates. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$x = \rho\sin\phi\cos\theta = {rho}\sin{phd}^\circ\cos{thd}^\circ \approx {X:num2}$,
$y = \rho\sin\phi\sin\theta = {rho}\sin{phd}^\circ\sin{thd}^\circ \approx {Y:num2}$,
$z = \rho\cos\phi = {rho}\cos{phd}^\circ \approx {Z:num2}$.
**$(x, y, z) \approx ({X:num2}, {Y:num2}, {Z:num2})$**.

drills.title: Radial integral over a ball
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\iiint_B {n}\,dV$ over the ball $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 \le {a}^2$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
In spherical coordinates $\sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2} = \rho$, so the integrand is a power of $\rho$; multiplied by the $\rho^2$ in $dV = \rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\theta\,d\phi$ it becomes $\rho^{{n2}}$:
$\displaystyle\int_0^\pi\sin\phi\,d\phi\int_0^{2\pi}d\theta\int_0^{{a}}\rho^{{n2}}\,d\rho = 2\cdot2\pi\cdot\frac{{a}^{{n3}}}{{n3}} \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Compute a Jacobian
drills.prompt: Find the Jacobian $\dfrac{\partial(x, y)}{\partial(u, v)}$ for $x = {a:coef}u^2 {b:signedcoef}v$, $y = {c:coef}uv$.
drills.solution:
$x_u = {a2}u$, $x_v = {b}$, $y_u = {c:coef}v$, $y_v = {c:coef}u$.
$\dfrac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)} = x_uy_v - x_vy_u = ({a2}u)({c:coef}u) - ({b})({c:coef}v) =$ **${k1}u^2 {k2:signedcoef}v$**.

drills.title: Area of a parallelogram by change of variables
drills.prompt: Let $R$ be the parallelogram bounded by $x {p:signedcoef}y = 0$, $x {p:signedcoef}y = {A}$, ${q:coef}x + y = 0$ and ${q:coef}x + y = {B}$. Using $u = x {p:signedcoef}y$ and $v = {q:coef}x + y$, find the area of $R$. (Exact fraction.)
drills.solution:
$\dfrac{\partial(u, v)}{\partial(x, y)} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & {p}\\ {q} & 1\end{vmatrix} = 1 - ({p})({q}) = {Ju}$, so $\left|\dfrac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right| = \dfrac{1}{|{Ju}|}$.
The new region is the rectangle $0 \le u \le {A}$, $0 \le v \le {B}$, so the area is $\dfrac{{A}\cdot{B}}{|{Ju}|} =$ **${area:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Evaluate a vector field
drills.prompt: For $\mathbf F(x, y) = \langle {a:coef}xy {b:signed},\; {c:coef}x^2 - y\rangle$, find $\mathbf F({x0}, {y0})$.

figure.caption: The field F, with the point marked

drills.solution:
Substitute $x = {x0}$, $y = {y0}$ into each component:
$P = ({a})({x0})({y0}) + ({b}) = {P0}$ and $Q = ({c})({x0})^2 - ({y0}) = {Q0}$.
**$\mathbf F({x0}, {y0}) = \langle {P0}, {Q0}\rangle$**.

drills.title: Gradient field
drills.prompt: Find the gradient field of $f(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2y {b:signedcoef}y^3 {c:signedcoef}x$.
drills.solution:
$\nabla f = \langle f_x, f_y\rangle$ with $f_x = {a2}xy {c:signed}$ and $f_y = {a:coef}x^2 {b3:signedcoef}y^2$.
**$\nabla f = \langle {a2}xy {c:signed},\; {a:coef}x^2 {b3:signedcoef}y^2\rangle$**.

drills.title: Scalar line integral along a segment
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_C({p:coef}x {q:signedcoef}y)\,ds$, where $C$ is the segment from $({x1}, {y1})$ to $({x2}, {y2})$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Parametrize $\mathbf r(t) = \langle {x1} + ({dx})t,\; {y1} + ({dy})t\rangle$, $0 \le t \le 1$, so $|\mathbf r'(t)| = \sqrt{({dx})^2 + ({dy})^2} \approx {L:num4}$.
The integrand is linear in $t$, so $\int_0^1 f(\mathbf r(t))\,dt$ is its value at the midpoint $({mx}, {my})$: ${p}({mx}) + ({q})({my}) = {avgf}$.
Value $= {avgf}\cdot{L:num4} \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Work along a power curve
drills.prompt: Find the work done by $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}x^2,\; {b:coef}xy\rangle$ on a particle moving along $y = x^{n}$ from $(0, 0)$ to $(1, 1)$. (Exact fraction.)
drills.solution:
Parametrize $\mathbf r(t) = \langle t, t^{n}\rangle$, $0 \le t \le 1$, so $\mathbf r'(t) = \langle 1, {n}t^{{n} - 1}\rangle$ and $\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t)) = \langle {a:coef}t^2,\; {b:coef}t^{{n1}}\rangle$.
$\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf r' = {a:coef}t^2 + ({b})({n})\,t^{{nn}}$, so $W = \displaystyle\int_0^1\left({a:coef}t^2 + ({b})({n})\,t^{{nn}}\right)dt = \frac{{a}}{3} + \frac{{b}\cdot{n}}{{n2}} =$ **${W:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Find a potential function
drills.prompt: The field $\mathbf F = \langle {a2}x {b:signedcoef}y {d:signed},\; {b:coef}x {c2:signedcoef}y\rangle$ is conservative. Find a potential function $f(x, y)$.
drills.solution:
Check: $P_y = {b} = Q_x$. ✓ Integrate $P$ in $x$: $f = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}xy {d:signedcoef}x + g(y)$.
Then $f_y = {b:coef}x + g'(y)$ must equal ${b:coef}x {c2:signedcoef}y$, so $g'(y) = {c2}y$ and $g = {c:coef}y^2$.
**$f(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}xy {c:signedcoef}y^2 {d:signedcoef}x$** (plus any constant).

drills.title: Fundamental theorem for line integrals
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r$ for $\mathbf F = \langle {a2}xy,\; {a:coef}x^2 {b:signed}\rangle$, where $C$ is any path from $({x1}, {y1})$ to $({x2}, {y2})$.
drills.solution:
$P_y = {a2}x = Q_x$, so $\mathbf F$ is conservative, with potential $f = {a:coef}x^2y {b:signedcoef}y$ (check: $f_x = {a2}xy$, $f_y = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signed}$).
By the fundamental theorem: $f({x2}, {y2}) - f({x1}, {y1}) = {fB} - ({fA}) =$ **{W}**.

drills.title: Green's theorem on a rectangle
drills.prompt: Use Green's theorem to evaluate $\displaystyle\oint_C {a:coef}xy\,dx + ({b:coef}x^2 {c:signedcoef}x)\,dy$, where $C$ is the boundary of the rectangle $[0, {A}]\times[0, {B}]$, counterclockwise.
drills.solution:
$Q_x - P_y = ({b2}x {c:signed}) - ({a:coef}x) = {k:coef}x {c:signed}$.
$\displaystyle\iint_R({k:coef}x {c:signed})\,dA = {k}\cdot\frac{{A}^2}{2}\cdot{B} + ({c})\cdot{A}\cdot{B} =$ **{ans}**.

drills.title: Area of a triangle with Green's theorem
drills.prompt: Use $A = \tfrac12\oint_C x\,dy - y\,dx$ to find the area of the triangle with vertices $O(0, 0)$, $P({x1}, {y1})$, $Q({x2}, {y2})$ (traversed $O \to P \to Q \to O$, which is counterclockwise).
drills.solution:
On a segment from $(x_a, y_a)$ to $(x_b, y_b)$, $\int x\,dy - y\,dx = x_ay_b - x_by_a$. The two sides through $O$ contribute 0.
The side $P \to Q$ contributes $({x1})({y2}) - ({x2})({y1}) = {cr}$.
$A = \tfrac12\cdot{cr} =$ **{area}**.

drills.title: Compute a curl
drills.prompt: Find $\operatorname{curl}\mathbf F$ for $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}xy {p:signedcoef}z,\; {b:coef}yz,\; {c:coef}xz\rangle$.
drills.solution:
With $P = {a:coef}xy {p:signedcoef}z$, $Q = {b:coef}yz$, $R = {c:coef}xz$:
$\mathbf i$: $R_y - Q_z = 0 - ({b})y$; $\mathbf j$: $P_z - R_x = {p} - ({c})z$; $\mathbf k$: $Q_x - P_y = 0 - ({a})x$.
**$\operatorname{curl}\mathbf F = \langle {nb:coef}y,\; {p} {nc:signedcoef}z,\; {na:coef}x\rangle$**.

drills.title: Compute a divergence
drills.prompt: Find $\operatorname{div}\mathbf F$ for $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}x^2y,\; {b:coef}yz^2,\; {c:coef}xz\rangle$.
drills.solution:
$\operatorname{div}\mathbf F = P_x + Q_y + R_z = {a2}xy + ({b})z^2 + ({c})x$.
**$\operatorname{div}\mathbf F = {a2}xy {b:signedcoef}z^2 {c:signedcoef}x$**.

drills.title: Normal vector to a parametric surface
drills.prompt: For $\mathbf r(u, v) = \langle u + v,\; {a:coef}u^2,\; {b:coef}v^2\rangle$, find the normal vector $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$ at $u = {u0}$, $v = {v0}$.
drills.solution:
$\mathbf r_u = \langle 1,\; 2({a})u,\; 0\rangle = \langle 1, {ru2}, 0\rangle$ and $\mathbf r_v = \langle 1,\; 0,\; 2({b})v\rangle = \langle 1, 0, {rv3}\rangle$ at the point.
$\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v = \langle ({ru2})({rv3}) - 0,\; 0 - (1)({rv3}),\; 0 - ({ru2})(1)\rangle =$ **$\langle {N1}, {N2}, {N3}\rangle$**.

drills.title: Surface area of a cone
drills.prompt: Find the area of the cone $z = {k:coef}\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$ between $z = 0$ and $z = {h}$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Parametrize $\mathbf r(r, \theta) = \langle r\cos\theta,\; r\sin\theta,\; {k:coef}r\rangle$ with $0 \le r \le {R}$ (since $z = {h}$ when $r = {R}$), $0 \le \theta \le 2\pi$.
$\mathbf r_r\times\mathbf r_\theta = \langle -{k:coef}r\cos\theta,\; -{k:coef}r\sin\theta,\; r\rangle$, of length $r\sqrt{1 + {k}^2}$.
$A = \displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{{R}}r\sqrt{1 + {k}^2}\,dr\,d\theta = \pi\cdot{R}^2\sqrt{1 + {k}^2} \approx$ **{A:num2}**.

drills.title: Flux through a slanted triangle
drills.prompt: Find the flux of $\mathbf F = \langle x, y, z\rangle$ upward through the part of the plane $\dfrac{x}{{a}} + \dfrac{y}{{b}} + \dfrac{z}{{c}} = 1$ in the first octant. (Exact or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Write the plane as $z = g(x, y) = {c}\left(1 - \frac{x}{{a}} - \frac{y}{{b}}\right)$, so $g_x = -\frac{{c}}{{a}}$ and $g_y = -\frac{{c}}{{b}}$.
Upward flux integrand: $-Pg_x - Qg_y + R = \frac{{c}}{{a}}x + \frac{{c}}{{b}}y + {c}\left(1 - \frac{x}{{a}} - \frac{y}{{b}}\right) = {c}$, a constant.
The shadow is a right triangle with legs {a} and {b}, area $\frac{{a}\cdot{b}}{2}$, so the flux is ${c}\cdot\frac{{a}\cdot{b}}{2} =$ **{flux}**.

drills.title: Surface integral over a hemisphere
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\iint_S({p} + {q:coef}z)\,dS$, where $S$ is the upper hemisphere $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = {a}^2$, $z \ge 0$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Parametrize with spherical angles: $z = {a}\cos\phi$ and $dS = {a}^2\sin\phi\,d\phi\,d\theta$ for $0 \le \phi \le \frac\pi2$.
$\iint_S {p}\,dS = {p}\cdot2\pi\cdot{a}^2 \approx {t1:num2}$ (the area of the hemisphere is $2\pi a^2$), and $\iint_S {q:coef}z\,dS = {q}\cdot\pi\cdot{a}^3 \approx {t2:num2}$.
Total $\approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Circulation by Stokes' theorem
drills.prompt: Use Stokes' theorem to evaluate $\displaystyle\oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r$ for $\mathbf F = \langle -{a:coef}y^3,\; {b:coef}x^3,\; z\rangle$, where $C$ is the circle $x^2 + y^2 = {R}^2$ in the plane $z = {h}$, counterclockwise seen from above. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\operatorname{curl}\mathbf F = \langle 0,\; 0,\; 3({b})x^2 + 3({a})y^2\rangle$. Use the flat disk at height {h} with $\mathbf n = \mathbf k$.
Over a disk of radius $R$, $\iint x^2\,dA = \iint y^2\,dA = \frac{\pi R^4}{4}$, so the flux of the curl is $3({b} + {a})\cdot\frac{\pi\cdot{R}^4}{4} \approx$ **{ans:num2}**. (The height {h} does not matter.)

drills.title: Divergence theorem on a box
drills.prompt: Use the Divergence theorem to find the outward flux of $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}x^2,\; {b:coef}y^2,\; {c:coef}z^2\rangle$ through the surface of the box $[0, {A}]\times[0, {B}]\times[0, {C}]$.
drills.solution:
$\operatorname{div}\mathbf F = {a2}x + ({b2})y + ({c2})z$.
$\displaystyle\iiint {a2}x\,dV = {a2}\cdot\frac{{A}^2}{2}\cdot{B}\cdot{C}$, and similarly for the other terms. Adding:
${a}\cdot{A}^2\cdot{B}\cdot{C} + ({b})\cdot{A}\cdot{B}^2\cdot{C} + ({c})\cdot{A}\cdot{B}\cdot{C}^2 =$ **{ans}**.

drills.title: Divergence theorem on a ball
drills.prompt: Find the outward flux of $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}x + y^2,\; {b:coef}y + z^2,\; {c:coef}z + x^2\rangle$ through the sphere $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = {R}^2$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\operatorname{div}\mathbf F = {a} {b:signed} {c:signed} = {d}$ (the squared terms have zero partial derivatives in their own slots).
By the Divergence theorem the flux is ${d}\cdot\frac43\pi\cdot{R}^3 \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Gauss's law
drills.prompt: A point charge of {qn} nC sits inside a closed surface (a sphere of radius {r} cm around it). Using $\varepsilon_0 = 8.854\times10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N·m}^2)$, find the electric flux through the surface in N·m²/C (3 significant figures).
drills.solution: By Gauss's law the flux is $Q_{\text{enc}}/\varepsilon_0$, whatever the radius: $\dfrac{{qn}\times10^{-9}}{8.854\times10^{-12}} \approx$ **{flux:sig3}** N·m²/C.
